title: S3 And CloudFront Drill
intro: Twelve scenario questions on S3 storage classes, bucket security and CloudFront behaviour. Answer cold — the explanation appears after each choice.
footer: Drawn from Lab 06 — Static site on S3 behind CloudFront. Reference notes: exam-notes.md
notes_intro: Twelve SAA-C03-style questions on object storage, lifecycle policy and content delivery, then the traps and reference tables. Answers are at the bottom — try them cold first.

questions.q: A static website is served by CloudFront from an S3 origin. Security requires that the bucket never be publicly accessible, while the site stays reachable. What should be configured?
options: Enable S3 static website hosting and make the bucket public
Use Origin Access Control and a bucket policy naming the CloudFront service principal
Place the bucket in a private subnet
Use a bucket ACL granting read to AuthenticatedUsers
questions.why: Origin Access Control signs origin requests with SigV4, and the bucket policy allows s3:GetObject to the CloudFront service principal conditioned on the specific distribution ARN. All four public-access blocks stay on. S3 is not in a VPC, so subnets are irrelevant; AuthenticatedUsers means any AWS user anywhere, which is a classic wrong answer.

questions.q: A CloudFront distribution returns 403 Access Denied for a URL path that does not exist in the S3 bucket, instead of a 404. Why?
options: The distribution is misconfigured and must be redeployed
S3 returns 403 rather than 404 for a missing key when the caller lacks s3:ListBucket
CloudFront caches 404 responses as 403
The bucket policy is missing s3:GetObject
questions.why: S3 deliberately returns 403 for a nonexistent key when the caller has no s3:ListBucket permission — revealing whether an object exists would itself leak information. A CloudFront custom error response mapping 403 to your 404 page is the standard fix, and this trips people constantly when debugging static sites.

questions.q: Data must be retained for compliance for seven years, is essentially never accessed, and a retrieval time of twelve hours is acceptable. Which storage class minimises cost?
options: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
questions.why: Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 storage, designed for long-term retention with retrieval measured in hours and a 180-day minimum duration. Glacier Instant Retrieval costs more because it offers millisecond access. Standard-IA is far more expensive for data never read. Intelligent-Tiering suits unknown or changing access patterns, not a known-cold one.

questions.q: An application's access pattern is unpredictable — some objects are read constantly, others not for months, and it changes over time. Which storage class is appropriate?
options: S3 Standard for everything
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 One Zone-IA
A lifecycle policy moving everything to Glacier after 30 days
questions.why: Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers automatically based on observed usage, for a small per-object monitoring fee and no retrieval charges in the frequent and infrequent tiers. Whenever a question describes an access pattern as unknown, unpredictable or changing, this is the intended answer.

questions.q: After uploading a corrected index.html to the origin bucket, viewers still receive the old content. What explains this?
options: S3 is eventually consistent for overwrites
Edge locations serve the cached object until its TTL expires or an invalidation is issued
The bucket policy caches the old object
Versioning is serving the previous version
questions.why: CloudFront caches at edge locations for the TTL set by the cache policy — with CachingOptimized the default is 24 hours. Uploading to the origin does not notify the edges. Either invalidate the path or, better, use versioned object names so every deploy is a new object and no invalidation is needed. S3 has been strongly consistent since 2020.

questions.q: A bucket has versioning enabled. A user deletes an object. What actually happens?
options: The object and all its versions are permanently removed
A delete marker becomes the current version and previous versions remain
The object moves to Glacier automatically
The delete is rejected until versioning is suspended
questions.why: A delete on a versioned bucket writes a delete marker as the new current version; every prior version remains and is billable. Removing the delete marker restores the object. This also means a versioned bucket is not empty just because objects look deleted — which is why teardown must remove versions and delete markers.

questions.q: Content must be served only to users who have paid, with access expiring after 24 hours. What is the appropriate CloudFront mechanism?
options: Origin Access Control
Signed URLs or signed cookies
A bucket policy restricting by IP address
Geo-restriction
questions.why: Signed URLs (one file) and signed cookies (many files or a whole area of a site) grant time-limited access to specific content. OAC controls how CloudFront reaches the origin, not who may reach CloudFront. Geo-restriction filters by country, not by entitlement.

questions.q: An S3 bucket in ap-southeast-2 serves large files to users in Europe, who report slow uploads. Which feature most directly addresses upload speed?
options: CloudFront with a longer TTL
S3 Transfer Acceleration
Cross-Region Replication
Multipart download
questions.why: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads to the nearest CloudFront edge and carries them over the AWS backbone to the bucket, which helps most over long distances. CloudFront accelerates downloads, not uploads. Cross-Region Replication copies objects after they arrive, so it does not help the upload itself.

questions.q: Which statement about S3 One Zone-IA is correct?
options: It replicates across three availability zones like Standard
It stores data in a single AZ and is unsuitable for data that cannot be recreated
It has the same durability as Standard but slower retrieval
It is the cheapest class for archival data
questions.why: One Zone-IA stores data in a single availability zone: roughly 20% cheaper than Standard-IA, and the data is lost if that AZ is destroyed. It suits easily recreatable data such as derived thumbnails or secondary copies — never the only copy of anything important.

questions.q: A company wants to ensure no bucket in the account can ever be made public, even if someone later attaches a permissive bucket policy. What provides this?
options: A lifecycle policy
S3 Block Public Access settings at the account level
Bucket versioning
Default encryption
questions.why: Block Public Access is a backstop that overrides bucket policies and ACLs — with it enabled, a policy granting public access is simply refused. Applied at the account level it covers every bucket including future ones. This is the single most effective control against accidental S3 exposure.

questions.q: CloudFront must serve content over HTTPS using a custom domain name. Where must the ACM certificate be requested?
options: In the same region as the origin bucket
In us-east-1, regardless of where other resources are
In any region, CloudFront replicates it
Certificates cannot be used with CloudFront
questions.why: A certificate used by CloudFront must be in us-east-1 (N. Virginia), because CloudFront is a global service managed from that region. A certificate for an Application Load Balancer, by contrast, must be in the load balancer's own region. This asymmetry is a reliable exam detail.

questions.q: What is the main cost difference between a CloudFront cache hit and a cache miss?
options: A hit costs more because edge storage is billed
A miss adds an origin request and origin data transfer on top of the edge delivery
There is no cost difference
A miss is free because the origin serves it
questions.why: A hit is served from the edge and costs the request plus data transfer out. A miss adds an S3 GET request and origin-to-edge transfer. This is why cache hit ratio is the main CloudFront cost lever — and why offloading traffic from the origin is a cost benefit as much as a latency one.
